item.title: Global experts seek Cambrian clues in central China's Hunan
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
Experts attend academic discussions on the Cambrian explosion and mass extinction, in Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture, central China's Hunan Province, Nov. 5, 2026. More than 160 scholars and researchers from China, the United States, Canada, Russia and other countries have recently wrapped up joint field work and academic discussions on the Cambrian explosion and mass extinction in Hunan Province, according to the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS). It was the first time Chinese and foreign experts had visited the Huayuan biota fossil site since research on it was published in January, as they sought clues to the Cambrian explosion and the mass extinction that followed. The site lies in Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture in Hunan. (Xinhua/Xue Yuge) CHANGSHA, Nov. 8 (Xinhua) -- More than 160 scholars and researchers from China, the United States, Canada, Russia and other countries have recently wrapped up joint field work and academic discussions on the Cambrian explosion and mass extinction in central China's Hunan Province, according to the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS). It was the first time Chinese and foreign experts had visited the Huayuan biota fossil site since research on it was published in January, as they sought clues to the Cambrian explosion and the mass extinction that followed. The site lies in Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture in Hunan. Concluding their work on Friday, the experts agreed that the Huayuan biota dates from just after the Sinsk mass extinction, fills a global gap in Cambrian Stage 4 soft-bodied fossil records, and is a valuable repository for studying the early evolution of life on Earth. It falls chronologically between the peak of the Cambrian explosion, represented by the Chengjiang biota, and the later Burgess Shale, documenting marine life after the Sinsk mass extinction. Over 500 million years ago, the Cambrian explosion gave rise to almost all animal phyla on Earth. It was followed by the Sinsk mass extinction, which wiped out countless early animals. Limited fossil evidence had long constrained scientists' understanding of the catastrophe and how life had recovered afterward. Research on the Huayuan biota, published in the journal Nature earlier this year, for the first time revealed the impact of this mass extinction on Earth's biosphere. Zhu Maoyan, a CAS academician and researcher at the Nanjing Institute of Geology and Palaeontology, located in east China, led the research endeavor. His team conducted five years of systematic excavations at the Renkupo section in Mozi Village, Huayuan County. They collected more than 50,000 fossil specimens and identified 153 animal species, nearly six-tenths of them new, bringing to light a fossil trove that had lain buried for hundreds of millions of years. Over 500 million years ago, the Xiangxi region was a deep-marine slope environment that provided exceptional conditions for preserving fine anatomical details. Earlier studies relied largely on fossils of shallow-water shelly animals, leading researchers to infer that marine life became scarce after the Sinsk mass extinction, Zhu said. The abundant fossils of the Huayuan biota have amended that view and provided solid field evidence for deep-water refugia, he said. Deep waters may have buffered the effects of the catastrophe, allowing some organisms to survive and preserving lineages for subsequent evolution, Zhu explained. "This fossil site is very special. You can find fossils very quickly here," said John Paterson, a professor at Australia's University of New England, at the Renkupo section. "Here, fossils are abundant, and the diversity is remarkable." He said the site offered ample material for research, with many species belonging to previously unknown groups. Representative taxa in the Huayuan biota closely match discoveries from the Burgess Shale in Canada. This particularly interested Jean-Bernard Caron, a researcher at Canada's Royal Ontario Museum. After reading about the findings in Nature, he hoped to visit the excavation site and examine the evidence firsthand. "I am excited to see this whole assemblage of fossils representing different groups of organisms. I have already seen many of these groups at fossil sites in the Burgess Shale in Canada," Caron said. He suggested that although these organisms inhabited widely separated seas during the Cambrian, they had originated earlier and could disperse between regions. Rather than individual animals swimming long distances, their larvae were more likely spread by ocean currents, he said. This process unfolded over immense spans of geological time and demonstrated that these organisms shared ancient common ancestors. Douglas Erwin, an external professor at the Santa Fe Institute in the United States, said the fossils from the Huayuan biota were exquisitely preserved, retaining fine internal anatomical structures. Their occurrence in deep-water facies deposited after the Sinsk mass extinction indicated that deep-water organisms had a better chance of surviving the catastrophe than shallow-water groups, he added. Zhu said research on the Huayuan biota was only just beginning, with many unknown taxa in the collections still awaiting investigation. The team will pursue multidisciplinary research to clarify the extent of the Sinsk mass extinction's impact, investigate how deep-water refugia formed, and reconstruct changes in ancient marine ecosystems, Zhu added. ■ This photo shows a trilobite fossil displayed at the exhibition hall of Huayuan biota in Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture, central China's Hunan Province, Nov. 4, 2026. item.title: Chinese motorcycle brands rev up European market, forging deeper industrial ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
* According to the China Chamber of Commerce for Motorcycle, China's exports of complete motorcycles to Europe reached approximately 1.298 billion U.S. dollars in the first seven months of 2026, up 17.17 percent year on year. * European industry insiders attribute the growing appeal of Chinese motorcycle brands to improvements in product quality, stronger innovation capabilities and greater exposure through international racing events. * As Chinese motorcycle manufacturers strengthen their technological capabilities and expand their presence in Europe, opportunities are also emerging for Chinese and European companies to deepen cooperation across the supply chain. MILAN, Italy, Nov. 8 (Xinhua) -- From conventional combustion-engine motorcycles to electric two-wheelers, Chinese companies showcased their latest models and technological innovations at the 83rd International Two-Wheeler Exhibition (EICMA 2026) in the Italian city of Milan, drawing remarkable interest from European dealers, industry professionals and consumers. The growing presence of Chinese brands at EICMA reflects their expanding footprint in Europe, where exports have continued to rise and brand recognition has improved. Through international motorcycle racing and localized operations, Chinese manufacturers are moving beyond product exports to build stronger brands and establish a deeper foothold in the European market. Industry insiders say the development of China's motorcycle industry is also creating new opportunities for Chinese and European companies to expand their markets and deepen supply chain cooperation. EXPANDING PRESENCE IN EUROPE According to the China Chamber of Commerce for Motorcycle (CCCM), China's exports of complete motorcycles to Europe reached approximately 1.298 billion U.S. dollars in the first seven months of 2026, up 17.17 percent year on year. Zhang Hongbo, secretary-general of the CCCM, told Xinhua that while Italy, Spain, Germany and France remain traditional markets for Chinese motorcycles, Chinese brands have also made significant inroads into markets in Central and Eastern Europe and Southern Europe, including Poland, the Czech Republic and Portugal, over the past two years. Figures released by Anesdor, the association representing Spain's motorcycle sector, show that Chinese brands' share of the Spanish motorcycle market has increased significantly in recent years, reaching 28 percent in the first half of 2026. In Portugal, Chinese brands CFMOTO, Voge and Zontes ranked fourth, fifth and sixth, respectively, in new motorcycle registrations in 2025, according to data from the Portuguese Automobile Association (ACAP). CFMOTO registrations surged 81.2 percent year on year, while Voge and Zontes recorded increases of 21.4 percent and 23.5 percent, respectively. Zhang also noted that average export prices of Chinese motorcycles to Europe have risen steadily this year, reflecting a shift in their competitive edge from price advantages toward product quality and overall value. GROWING COMPETITIVENESS European industry insiders attribute the growing appeal of Chinese motorcycle brands to improvements in product quality, stronger innovation capabilities and greater exposure through international racing events. Jose Maria Riano, secretary general of Anesdor, told Xinhua that the growing popularity of Chinese motorcycle brands reflects their ability to offer "a quality product at a very competitive price." Nicolas, a Danish dealer for ZXMOTO, said Chinese manufacturers are more flexible in decision-making than some traditional European counterparts and show a strong willingness to innovate and continuously improve their products and technologies. He said he believes ZXMOTO has the potential to rank among the top five brands in Denmark's lightweight motorcycle segment. Antonio Giordano, a motorcycle dealer in Naples, Italy, said Chinese brands "not only represent the present, but also the future." He added that improvements in product quality have made them increasingly competitive with established European manufacturers. International racing has also emerged as an important platform for Chinese brands to raise their profile and build their reputations in Europe. In 2026, Chinese brands such as ZXMOTO and CFMOTO achieved notable results in various international motorcycle competitions. Portuguese motorsports commentator Rui Belmonte told Xinhua that these breakthroughs demonstrated China's progress in motorcycle performance, engine development and manufacturing technology, while also reflecting a broader transformation of Chinese manufacturers from producers traditionally associated with low-cost commuter models into makers of high-performance, technologically advanced motorcycles. He said Chinese motorcycles are increasingly meeting international standards in technology, design, reliability and performance, with some models now capable of competing with or even outperforming Japanese rivals while retaining a significant price advantage. NEW COOPERATION OPPORTUNITIES As Chinese motorcycle manufacturers strengthen their technological capabilities and expand their presence in Europe, opportunities are also emerging for Chinese and European companies to deepen cooperation across the supply chain. In July, CFMOTO signed a strategic cooperation agreement with Italian braking system manufacturer Brembo. The two companies will collaborate on product development and technological innovation, among other areas. Zhang said the partnership illustrates how the development of China's motorcycle industry is creating new business opportunities for European motorcycle and component manufacturers. As Chinese-made medium- and large-displacement motorcycles undergo rapid upgrades, demand for high-end European components, including braking and suspension systems, tires, electronic control systems and precision engine parts, continues to increase, creating greater scope for supply chain cooperation, he said. Fabrizio Cazzoli, global sales and after-sales director of Italian motorcycle manufacturer Ducati, told Xinhua that the development of China's motorcycle industry is benefiting the industry as a whole by bringing more people into motorcycling and generating greater interest in motorcycle culture. Ducati already works with numerous Chinese partners and hopes to further strengthen its presence in the Chinese market and deepen ties with its local partners, Cazzoli said. "I think all brands together are good for the market," he said, adding that they are all motorcycle manufacturers and look forward to exchanging ideas and experience. International racing is another area offering considerable potential for cooperation. Desiree Cherici, team manager of Spain's FUTUROTEL FACE RACING team in the FIM MotoJunior World Championship, told Xinhua that European racing teams, with their well-established rider development systems, should recognize the rapid advances in China's motorcycle industry. "We need to build connections with China so that we can grow alongside the emerging motorcycles and new brands," she said. Cherici said she expects more Chinese companies to enter international racing championships, adding that their participation could also create opportunities for European teams to grow. "I think this is beneficial for both sides," she said. (Video reporters: Zhang Huan, Gao Jingyan; Video editors: Wang Han, Luo Hui, Zhang Yuhong, Zhang Yichi, Liu Yutian) ■

item.title: China Focus: Daoist culture attracts young followers worldwide
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
HANGZHOU, Nov. 8 (Xinhua) -- In the morning mist on Wudang Mountain in central China's Hubei Province, a young Spaniard dressed in a traditional Daoist robe slowly performed Tai Chi. Each measured movement of his hands and feet conveyed a sense of composure. Alex Mieza recently shared a video of this performance on his Instagram account. "Tai Chi isn't just slow movement. It's a quiet way to build real internal strength," he wrote. The post garnered more than 3,000 likes and over 100 comments. One Spanish-speaking user described the practice as beautiful, noting that although it looked like dancing, it required considerable strength and concentration. The post offers a glimpse into growing international interest in Daoism, a Chinese religious and philosophical tradition featuring teachings on balance, harmony and living in accordance with nature, which are attracting a new generation of followers and enthusiasts worldwide. On social media platforms like TikTok, Instagram and YouTube, more videos featuring traditional wellness practices such as Tai Chi, Qigong and Baduanjin, as well as Daoist philosophy, are posted, reaching audiences far beyond China. Accounts dedicated to these subjects are gaining traction in English-, Spanish- and French-speaking communities, with practitioners and content creators introducing the Daoist traditions via physical exercises and philosophical discussions. At the 6th International Daoism Forum, which concluded on Friday in Hangzhou, capital of east China's Zhejiang Province, delegates explored why Daoism resonates with young people navigating the pressures and uncertainties of modern life. Under the theme "Cultivating Virtue Through the Dao, Fostering Harmony Under Heaven," participants discussed five topics: contemporary value and global transmission of Daoist culture, technological development, healthy living, and talent cultivation. For Lee Moden, vice president of the British Daoist Association, Daoist culture offers people an opportunity to slow down and reconnect with themselves. "It provides a space for them to begin to settle down and realize the value of what that space helps them realize in themselves," Moden said. Moden added that young people today are often caught in a cycle of constantly feeling compelled to respond to messages, promote themselves on social media and create new identities. Daoist cultivation, by contrast, allows people to let go of constant striving and the constant personal desire to achieve all the time, Moden said. For Fan Ao, dean of academic affairs at Shanghai Taoist College, located in east China, a key source of Daoism's appeal lies in its inclusiveness. In a world where different cultures constantly interact and sometimes clash, young people need ways to navigate diversity, with confidence in their own culture and inclusiveness toward other cultures, Fan said. Chen Zhiwei, honorary president of the youth group of the Taoist Federation of Singapore, sees Daoism's appeal in more practical terms. Many young people face insecurity and stress in their daily lives and Daoist approaches offer ways to cope with pressure and anxiety, Chen said. "Daoism is not simply about worshiping deities with incense. If you truly understand the word 'Dao,' it is a principle that keeps you healthy, long-lived and happy," he said. For many younger followers and enthusiasts, approaching Daoism does not necessarily mean formally adopting the religion. Some are drawn to its physical practices, while others explore its philosophy as a way to tackle real-world issues. In Singapore, the Daoist community has been exploring ways to engage younger generations, Chen said. Initiatives include digitizing resources, making temple activities more youth-friendly, and simplifying programs to lower the threshold to participation. Moden said short videos could help attract young people to Daoism. "If these videos help people become curious, if they think this philosophy is interesting, or they see Tai Chi, Qigong and find it intriguing, that is good. It acts as a gateway," he said. But social media cannot replace teachers and cannot replace an environment for cultivation, Moden noted. Fan stressed the importance of continuous study of classical texts rather than relying solely on fragmented online content. Shanghai Taoist College, notably, has been working to interpret Daoist classics in contemporary language, he added. ■

item.title: Economic Watch: Beyond market size, European firms tap China's growth, innovation potential
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
SHANGHAI, Nov. 8 (Xinhua) -- Amid dazzling displays at the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), a truck-sized turn-mill machine stands quietly, its computer-controlled spindle whirring. Without flashy decorations, the machine still draws curious crowds. The attraction is a piece of precision machinery from an Austrian "hidden champion" WFL, shown under the expo's "deep-tech" label. Weighing over 20 tonnes, the machine began its journey in August, crossing oceans and moving between trucks and shipping containers before arriving at the Port of Shanghai, host city of the CIIE -- a major platform for China to open its vast market to the world. Why go to such lengths? Mayr Günther Franz Josef, general manager of WFL, told Xinhua that participating in the CIIE offers a chance to gain firsthand insights into China's rapidly upgrading high-end manufacturing sector and to forge closer ties with industrial partners across the Asia-Pacific region. The company had another goal in mind: to make the machine's journey a one-way trip. As hoped, it found a buyer just three days into the expo. Across the exhibition floor, European companies are deepening their engagement with China, drawn not only by the sheer size of its market but increasingly by opportunities arising from industrial upgrading, evolving consumer demand and a vibrant innovation ecosystem. MORE THAN A VAST MARKET China's pursuit of high-quality development, coupled with rising living standards, has fueled increasingly sophisticated demand for industrial and consumer products, opening up new avenues of growth for businesses worldwide. "As China's manufacturing capabilities continue to advance, demand for high-end machine tools and other sophisticated industrial equipment is growing," said Zheng Xiaoli, a representative at WFL's booth. The company's machine tools are used to manufacture complex, high-precision components for industries including aviation, aerospace and shipbuilding. The changing composition of their Chinese clientele offers a glimpse into that transformation. "Our customers in China used to be mainly state-owned enterprises and foreign-invested companies. Now, a growing number of private Chinese manufacturers seeking quality products are investing in our high-end machinery," said Zheng. China's accelerating green transition and digital transformation are also creating fresh opportunities for European suppliers of advanced technologies and specialized materials. For AMORNEX, a joint venture between Luxembourg-based steelmaker ArcelorMittal and China Oriental Group, the booming electric vehicle industry in China is driving demand for advanced materials. Jurgen Cobbaut, the company's chief marketing officer, told Xinhua that some high-performance electric motors in Chinese EVs require materials with exceptional strength and efficiency, which plays to the company's strengths. "It's not only the volume, but also the level of sophistication. That is what really makes it interesting," Cobbaut said of the Chinese market. The shift toward more sophisticated demand extends to consumer markets, where changing lifestyles and rising expectations are also inspiring product innovation. German cleaning equipment manufacturer Kärcher, for example, developed a compact, foldable pressure washer for cleaning bicycles, cars and camping gear, tapping into Chinese consumers' growing enthusiasm for outdoor activities. Originally designed for the Chinese market, the product has since been rolled out globally. "Chinese consumers today are much more sophisticated. They're looking for products that fit their lifestyles," said Bernd Rützler, an executive vice president of Alfred Kärcher GmbH & Co. KG. INNOVATION ENGINE Beyond evolving demand, China's innovation capabilities, underpinned by its extensive supply chains and fast-evolving market, are becoming powerful draws for European companies. "China has always been one of our most important strategic markets globally. What has changed is the increasingly multifaceted role China plays," said Liu Ling, chief region leader of Philips China. For the Dutch health technology company, China is not only its second-largest market worldwide but also a "key supply-chain hub and engine of innovation." Increasingly, innovations developed in China are also finding their way into European companies' global product portfolios. Drawing on China's "strong industrial foundation, abundant innovation resources and diverse use cases," Schneider Electric has worked with Chinese partners to develop a range of proven, scalable solutions that are helping businesses across sectors become smarter, more efficient and greener, said Yin Zheng, executive vice president of China & East Asia Operations of Schneider Electric. In the medical equipment hall at the CIIE, widely regarded as one of the expo's most competitive sections, Swedish medical equipment manufacturer Elekta is showcasing its AI-powered AutoART adaptive radiotherapy solution. The system can shorten the adaptive radiotherapy process -- from imaging and treatment planning to treatment delivery -- to just 10 to 15 minutes. Developed in response to the demands of China's busy radiotherapy departments, this technology is intended for wider international use, according to Jin Jianxue, vice president and medical affairs director of Elekta China. COMPLEMENTARY STRENGTHS The CIIE offers a timely view of deepening business ties between China and Europe, as EU policymakers weigh trade issues with China. The deeper ties are rooted in strong complementarity between the two sides, said Shen Yi, an international relations scholar at Fudan University. As China seeks to upgrade its industries and improve living standards, it needs European products and expertise in areas such as advanced equipment, precision instruments, pharmaceuticals and professional services, Shen told Xinhua. Europe, in turn, stands to benefit from China's vast market, manufacturing capabilities and technological advances in sectors like batteries and solar power, he added. Illustrating such complementarity, Zhang Shuo, chief representative at the Beijing Representative Office of the Brussels-based European Automobile Manufacturers Association (ACEA), noted that Europe's century-old automotive industry has deep expertise in engineering, safety and environmental technologies, while China has taken the lead in batteries and electric mobility. Cooperation is also moving beyond the traditional model of importing finished vehicles or transferring technology toward closer integration of industrial supply chains and joint research and development, he told Xinhua at their booth. ACEA is attending this year's CIIE as an exhibitor for the first time, although its member companies have long been regular participants. Going forward, China has called for an "upward balance" in trade, achieved through greater openness and an expanding economic pie, rather than a "downward balance" caused by closing markets. Ultimately, openness remains a powerful draw. As Rützler put it: "We see China as a reliable market and a reliable partner. Its continued opening up gives us the confidence to invest more." ■

item.title: APEC-year momentum fuels robust CIIE presence as Asia-Pacific economies tap China's open market
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-08
SHANGHAI, Nov. 8 (Xinhua) -- As China hosts the 2026 APEC year, the ongoing ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) serves as a tangible demonstration of the Asia-Pacific pursuit of open regionalism, bringing together established multinationals, rising SMEs and industry innovators to turn China's enormous market potential into shared opportunities for the whole region. Running from Nov. 5 to 10 in Shanghai, the world's first national-level expo dedicated to imports has drawn wide-ranging delegations and exhibitors from across the Asia-Pacific. Southeast Asian players, including Thailand, Indonesia and Singapore, alongside economies in Oceania and Northeast Asia, have brought consumer goods, advanced technologies and innovative services to the exhibition halls. Paijit Viboontanasarn, vice chairman and secretary general of the Thai Chamber of Commerce in China, said in an interview with Xinhua that the CIIE offers Thai businesses a gateway to the Chinese market, helping smaller firms find customers and test business models while enabling larger companies to deepen cooperation. "Beyond securing orders, the CIIE allows businesses to test whether their products and business models appeal to Chinese consumers," Paijit said. He described the expo in three words: "unique," "opportunity," and "openness," citing its import focus, opportunities for businesses of all sizes, and participation from across the world. Thai brands are putting this into practice. Botanical fragrance maker Phutawan and snack producer MagMag are showcasing their signature products at this year's expo. "Trade goes both ways," said Nonthakogh Panyapadhm, founder and CEO of MagMag. "Business can last only if both sides benefit." Mark Lee, chairman of the Singapore Business Federation, noted that for Singapore businesses, the value of attending the CIIE "deepens over time." "Many of our companies begin by using the CIIE to build visibility and gather market insights. Over several years, those initial engagements can grow into distribution agreements, joint ventures, and in some cases, regional partnerships that extend beyond China into Southeast Asia," Lee told Xinhua. The federation is leading a 54-company Singapore delegation for the ninth consecutive edition of the expo. Samsung, the South Korean conglomerate, marks its ninth straight year at the CIIE. Zhang Daijun, senior vice president of Samsung China, pointed out that the group keeps expanding its high-end investment and local R&D footprint in China. "China's firm commitment to expanding high-standard opening up has created more opportunities for international enterprises, and provided a stable and predictable environment for their development, injecting greater certainty into global trade cooperation," Zhang said. From the Southern Hemisphere, Australian and New Zealand enterprises are also actively engaging with Chinese consumers via the expo. Rhys Roberts, national president and chair of the Australia China Business Council, said what matters most to Australian members is what happens after the expo. "Conversations that start on the show floor become distribution agreements, repeat orders and long-term partnerships, and that is where the real value lies," he said. Sanchia Yonge, chief executive of New Zealand Trade and Enterprise, regards the CIIE as a valuable opportunity for New Zealand exporters to showcase products, understand the evolving Chinese market, strengthen brand awareness, and connect with customers and partners for long-term growth. Blis Technologies, a New Zealand biotechnology company, is experiencing a new milestone this year, as it will have its own independent booth at the Shanghai expo. In just two years, sales of its oral probiotics products in China have exceeded 100,000 orders. It's very important to attend the expo on a regular basis because the Chinese market is changing quickly, said Scott Johnson, CEO of Blis Technologies. Humprey Arnaldo Russel, head of the ASEAN-China Research Center at the University of Indonesia, commented that the CIIE serves as a vital "gateway" for regional small and medium-sized enterprises to tap the Chinese market and build resilient trade networks amid shifting global dynamics. "China gives opportunities to countries all across the globe," he said. "We need an open system where people with small and medium-sized enterprises, whether in Africa, Indonesia, Vanuatu, or Fiji, have the opportunity to trade across the globe based on WTO rules."■

Published: 2026-11-08
BEIJING, Nov. 8 (Xinhua) -- The Communist Party of China (CPC), the world's largest governing party, has launched the process of electing delegates to its 21st national congress, which is scheduled to be held in the second half of 2027 in Beijing. An official from the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee has explained why the election matters, how it will be organized, and what standards eligible candidates must meet. Here is what to know about the election. The 21st CPC National Congress comes at a critical time when the CPC has been working to basically realize socialist modernization and heading toward the Second Centenary Goal. It will be a highly important meeting and an event of great political significance for both the Party and the country, as a new CPC Central Committee and a new CPC Central Commission for Discipline Inspection will be elected. The 2,360 delegates to be elected should be outstanding Party members who carry the trust of more than 101 million CPC members and over 5.4 million Party organizations as they fulfill their duties at the congress. The successful election of delegates and the completion of all tasks at the congress are vital to consolidating the Party's long-term governing position and enabling the Party to fully exercise its role as the leadership core. They are also closely linked to the prosperity and long-term stability of the Party and the country. The election should be a process of studying and implementing Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, particularly Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building. Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, has attached great importance to carrying out sound work related to the election. He heard multiple reports on this matter. He also presided over meetings of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, at which a circular on the election was deliberated and adopted. The key to ensuring the success of the election is upholding the Party's overall leadership and the centralized, unified leadership of the CPC Central Committee. Emphasis must be placed on examining candidates' political stance and awareness, as well as their capacity for political judgment, thinking and implementation. Their integrity and conduct must also be subject to strict scrutiny. The delegates elected should be well-structured in composition and broadly representative, drawing from a wide range of fields, including the economy, science and technology, national defense, law enforcement and the justice system, education, public communication, culture, health, sports and social administration. They should also include workers in new forms of employment. Front-line workers should account for an appropriate proportion of the delegates. Among delegates from provincial-level regions, central financial institutions and central state-owned enterprises in Beijing, Party members working on the front line should generally account for at least one-third. Among delegates from central Party and state departments, the proportion should generally be no less than 15 percent. In regions where the new economy and new forms of business are thriving and there are large numbers of workers in new forms of employment, outstanding Party members from among these workers should also be recommended as candidates. Particular attention should be paid to recommending model workers, farmers and professionals as candidates. Women Party members and Party members from ethnic minority groups should each make up a certain proportion of the delegates. Political, organizational and electoral disciplines must be strictly observed throughout the election process, with efforts made to prevent vote-buying and other electoral violations and strengthen oversight and enforcement. The electoral procedure consists of five steps: nomination of candidates, assessment of nominees by electoral units, formation of a preliminary list of candidates, formation of a preparatory list of candidates, and formal election. The delegates will be elected through a process in which the number of candidates must exceed the number of seats by more than 15 percent. The delegates elected will be vetted by a qualification review committee prior to the national congress. ■

item.title: Unswervingly dedicated to the people | Remain true to our original aspiration
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
In 2026, the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China was held in Beijing, focusing on persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance. From Stephen's insights on Party discipline and Qinling's ecological restoration, to Abuluoha's village access road, the CPC remains true to its original aspiration.

item.title: Xi votes in local legislative election in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, casts his ballot to elect deputies to the Xicheng district people's congress at the Huairentang polling station of the Zhongnanhai electoral district in Xicheng District of Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping cast his ballot at a polling station in Beijing on Friday to elect deputies to a local people's congress. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, voted at the Huairentang polling station of the Zhongnanhai electoral district in Xicheng District to elect deputies to the Xicheng district people's congress. Xi stressed efforts to practice whole-process people's democracy, uphold Party leadership, and strengthen oversight throughout the election process to ensure that deputies who meet the people's expectations are elected. Around 3:30 p.m. Friday, Xi arrived at the polling station, gave his voter registration card to staff for verification, and got a ballot. He cast his ballot after filling it. Noting that the election of deputies to people's congresses is an important foundation for upholding, improving and practicing the people's congress system, Xi underlined the need to give full play to democracy, strictly act in accordance with the law, and ensure that the election is carried out fairly and cleanly. On Friday afternoon, other senior Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi cast their ballots in person, while Han Zheng entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Former Chinese leader Hu Jintao also entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Friday saw people vote at 13,054 polling stations across Beijing to elect 4,898 new deputies to the people's congresses at the district level and 11,137 deputies to the township-level people's congresses. ■ Chinese Premier Li Qiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, casts his ballot to elect deputies to a local people's congress at the Ziguangge polling station of the Wenjin Street electoral district in Xicheng District of Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Huang Jingwen) Zhao Leji, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the National People's Congress (NPC) Standing Committee, casts his ballot to elect deputies to a local people's congress at the Great Hall of the People polling station of the Zhongnanhai electoral district in Xicheng District of Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Ling) Wang Huning, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) National Committee, casts his ballot to elect deputies to a local people's congress at the Huairentang polling station of the Zhongnanhai electoral district in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Shen Hong) Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and a member of the CPC Central Committee Secretariat, casts his ballot to elect deputies to a local people's congress at the Huairentang polling station of the Zhongnanhai electoral district in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, casts his ballot to elect deputies to a local people's congress at the Ziguangge polling station of the Wenjin Street electoral district in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026.
